english.title: Attempt rape of a female under 16
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) attempted to rape **(..SPECIFY THE NAME OF THE GIRL..), a girl under 16 years of age
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
attempt to rape
a female under 16 years

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) THIS OFFENCE IS NOW OBSOLETE - now see H5655
(ii) For the wording of the substantive offence see H542.
(iii) Repealed by s.140 of and Schedule 7 to the Sexual Offences Act 2003
(iv) When using this offence wording to charge for an alleged crime committed prior to 27th August 1981, officers should be aware that the appropriate legislation is 'Contrary to Common Law' NOT 'section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981'.
(v) A prior conviction for an offence listed in Schedule 15 to the Sentencing Act 2020, may render the convicted person liable to a mandatory life sentence in relation to a second offence listed under that Schedule, as per section 273 (offender aged 18 or over but under 21 when convicted of the second offence or section 283 (offender aged 21 or over).
